scope: New task IDs created by upgraded DirectSheetsApi clients, including independent browsers and devices without Web Locks.
batch: AddNamedRange with deterministic ID/name derived from SHA-256(task ID)
anchor: Primary task sheet S1. The named range is a permanent create claim, not a pointer to the appended row.
on_collision: Google rejects the complete batch. Reread both task tabs and rerun the engine's three-way merge; never acknowledge the rejected batch. Different task contents remain an explicit conflict.
on_missing_claimed_row: If no colliding task row can be found, retain the local changes and report a data error. Do not remove the claim or append blindly.
on_lost_response: Read the remote task IDs before retrying. An already committed task is not appended again.
limitations: Not a compare-and-swap for edits to existing rows.
Legacy clients, third-party scripts and manual edits do not participate in this create protocol.
Deleting reserved named ranges removes the server create fence for their task IDs.
Web Locks remains an optimization within one browser; correctness of upgraded creates no longer relies on it.
server_probe: Two independent requests to an isolated native Google Sheet: one accepted, one rejected with 400, one appended row confirmed by reread.
